Treadmill Justice and the Case of the Missing Hero

It was a quiet Sunday in Quezon City. The kind of day when the silence feels suspicious. Marge was in the UK, helping Vana and Lily Bear settle into a new home. Simmy was out with her parents. 

And I—left to my own devices—found myself on the treadmill, not chasing fitness, but chasing justice… through the lens of The Equalizer.

There he was: Robert McCall. Ex-CIA, part-time vigilante, full-time demolisher of Russian syndicates. He didn’t ask for permission. He didn’t form a committee. He didn’t hold a press conference. He just walked into the room and made things… equal.

And I thought: We need a McCall.

Not for Hollywood. For the House of Representatives. For the DPWH. For the flood control program that’s drowning in more paperwork than water. For the independent commission that might—just might—uncover the real blueprint of corruption, etched not in concrete but in campaign donations and contractor kickbacks.

Imagine McCall in the Palace. Not as President—he’d never survive the selfies. But as Chair of the Independent Commission. 

He’d find the lawmaker hiding in the U.S. faster than you can say “subpoena.” He’d audit PhilHealth with a stopwatch. He’d ask one question: Are you helping the people, or helping yourself? And then he’d act accordingly—with a nail gun, if necessary.

But alas, McCall is fictional. Our heroes are confined to Netflix. The real ones are either retired, disillusioned, or stuck in traffic. 

Redemption? People are praying. But prayers don’t seem to penetrate the walls of power. Maybe they need a VPN.

So here I am, on Grandparents Day, praying on Pope Leo’s birthday, watching Denzel Washington do what no Filipino official dares to do: clean up without fear, without favor, and without a press release.

No more heroes here. Only in the movies.

Unless, of course, someone decides to step off the treadmill and into the fire.

#RelentlessForChange #SimmyInspires❤️ 
#LilyLoves😍 

Tony Leachon

3-DAY NATIONWIDE TRANSPORT STRIKE

LOOK: Transport group Manibela will hold a nationwide transport strike from Sept. 17 to 19 to protest the alleged corruption in the government.

"Excise tax ng diesel, napupunta lang pala sa luho ng mga anak ng pulitiko!" Manibela says.

"Hindi na tama na kami ang nagpapalamon at pumopondo sa karangyaan nila, na samantalang ang mga masang tsuper ay halos magdamag na kung bumiyahe kumita lang nang sapat para sa kanilang pamilya," it adds.

The group will also march to Rizal Park in Manila on Sept. 21 to call for accountability.

📸 Manibela/Facebook

DOMINICAN FAMILY FOR JUSTICE AND PEACE CALLS ON FILIPINOS TO JOIN SEPT. 21 ‘TRILLION-PESO MARCH’

READ: The Dominican Family for Justice, Peace and Care for Creation – Philippines has called for accountability over alleged “systemic and trillion-peso-scale corruption” in flood-control projects and urged Filipinos to join the “Trillion Peso March” at EDSA Shrine on Sept. 21.

“Ang pananatiling tahimik sa gitna ng mga kawalang-hustisya sa ating lipunan ang siyang nagbibigay-lakas sa mga tiwaling lider ng bayan upang magpatuloy sa pang-aabuso sa kanilang kapangyarihan,” the group said.

It also urged Congress to pursue hearings and hold officials, contractors, and other parties involved in the anomalous projects accountable.

The nationwide protest is set at 2 p.m. and will also be held in various parts of the country, the group said.
